grh_cf782f782e2aba5ac0fe.title: Nuptial Flight
paragraphs: A newlywed couple crossing a vast, empty stretch of highway are terrorized by three young men in a faster car who repeatedly cut them off and threaten them. The harassment exposes strains in the marriage and the bride's previously unrecognized terror of open country; even a remote service-station owner refuses to let them use his phone because he fears the local men. With nowhere to hide or get help, the couple finally turns the chase around and forces the pursuing car off the road. It overturns and burns, and the newlyweds choose to drive on rather than stop, grimly rationalizing what has happened.

This [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] broadcast aired on December 18, 1964. It is listed as episode 100 in the archive. [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Elliott Reid, Lesley Woods, Larry Robinson, Luis Van Rooten, and Marty Folia. Other credited names include Warren Somerville as director, Warren Somerville as producer, William Morn as writer, and Fred Foy as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 20 minutes.

grh_cf2a670c042316f3b802.title: Every Frame Has a Silver Lining
paragraphs: Harry follows a seemingly respectable family because a valuable picture in a silver frame appears to offer a profitable opportunity, only to discover that Helen and her supposed relatives are part of an opium-smuggling ring. Harry and Helen temporarily join forces, tie up the others and wait for the money, with Helen proposing that they become permanent partners. When police arrive, Harry switches sides without hesitation, claiming he forced Helen to reveal the gang and directing the officers to the smugglers and their drugs. He collects the government reward and later insists that he opposed narcotics on principle, while admitting the size of the reward made honesty particularly attractive.

grh_cfe1018b95713a2e09ab.title: An Average American Murder
paragraphs: Hardworking factory employee Sam Crawford comes home after an exhausting Friday of overtime, humiliation, drinking and a speeding arrest, already angry that the simple evening he planned with his wife Millie has been spoiled. Millie criticizes his temper and the way he makes life harder for himself, and their argument escalates over burned pork chops. Feeling mocked by everyone, Sam loses control and attacks her with a butcher knife. In prison he becomes a model inmate, but every Friday night he cries over the ordinary domestic life he destroyed in a moment of rage.

The surviving recording runs about 21 minutes.

grh_cfac3fd2aa27c2b03fe5.title: 5000 Pengoes and a Kiss
paragraphs: In postwar Hungary, singer Helena Bana hires Harry to get her across the closed border for 5,000 pengoes and a kiss. Rival fixer Zama betrays the scheme to the police, forcing Harry and Helena through barbed wire, patrols and gunfire. Harry finally holds a police inspector at gunpoint long enough for Helena to cross into Austria, while he stays behind and bargains away his automobile to buy his own escape. Helena later becomes a success abroad, but Harry remembers that even after collecting his promised kiss she dedicated a song to him about a rascal better off dead.

grh_cfbc12c8623b1a4b275d.title: A Girl a Guy and a Gob
paragraphs: Dorothy Duncan is engaged to respectable Stephen Herrick when exuberant sailor Coffee Cup enters her life and becomes a disruptive new friend. Coffee Cup's rough charm, Navy buddies and impulsive schemes repeatedly throw Dorothy and Stephen's courtship into confusion, and for a time he seems ready to compete for her himself. Realizing Dorothy truly loves Stephen, Coffee Cup steps aside, arranges and pays for their wedding, and heads back to duty after making sure the couple finally marries.
